summary.text: Ken Heuvelman is the Democratic candidate for Michigan House of Representatives District 64 in the November 3, 2026 general election, challenging incumbent Republican Rep. Joseph Pavlov.
A counselor who lives in Port Huron, he works in behavioral health and substance use disorder services.

paragraphs.text: Ken Heuvelman was born in Grand Rapids, Michigan, graduated from Linden High School, and attended Michigan State University.
He earned a graduate degree from Montana State University, Billings in 2016 and another from Walden University in 2022.
Ballotpedia lists affiliations with Port Huron Odyssey House, the St. Clair County Advisory Board of Health, St. Clair County Community Services, and Ad Populum Consulting & Counseling.

In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey, Heuvelman said he is a Limited License Professional Counselor with more than ten years in behavioral health, working as a family support program supervisor and as coordinator of a mobile overdose response team in St. Clair County.
He said he chairs the St. Clair County Substance Use Prevention, Treatment, and Recovery workgroup.
Heuvelman ran in the August 6, 2024 Democratic primary for District 64 and finished third with 755 votes, behind John Anter and Mathew Castillo.
He said in the 2024 survey that he stands for social and fiscal responsibility in government and evidence-based decision making.
